title: Colophon · Brett Boggs
description: How this site is made: the tools, the pipeline, and the weight of every page.
heading: How this site is made.
lede: The tools, the pipeline, and the weight of every page. Built by hand, hosted for nothing.

sections.heading: The stack
sections.body: Astro, fully static. There is no framework in the page and no CSS framework under it: plain CSS with custom properties, and TypeScript written for the one page that needs it. GSAP draws the front page's diagram and drives the film in the lab, and three.js turns the models. Fonts are self hosted: Archivo for display and reading, condensed on its width axis for headlines, and IBM Plex Mono for labels. A GitHub Action builds every push and GitHub Pages serves it under a domain from Namecheap, which puts the monthly bill at zero.

sections.heading: The film
sections.body: The Ridge, which opened the front page until October 2026 and now lives in the [lab](/lab/film/), was modelled and rendered in Blender with Cycles, 192 frames, on free CC0 assets from Poly Haven for the sky, the ground and the grass. A Node script runs the frames through sharp into WebP at two sizes with posters and a manifest. In the browser the frames decode into a canvas and the scroll position picks the frame, so the flyover runs at whatever speed you read.

sections.heading: The lab
sections.body: Each experiment brings its own engine. The MacArthur is a three.js orbit viewer over models built from public survey data. The Field is a WebGPU compute shader with a spring for every blade. The keepsake is an SVG drawn from a seed, so the same address always draws the same field. Everything that moves has a still or a fallback for browsers and people who would rather it did not.

sections.heading: Type and motion
sections.body: The look is a drawing set: a white sheet on an engineering grid, black ink, one signal orange, and blueprint blue for annotation. Headlines are Archivo pulled narrow on its width axis. Near the pointer the grid inks in, the bar reads out where you are on the sheet, and pages change under native cross-document view transitions, the bar holding still while the sheet underneath is swapped. Every motion on the site is switched off for a reduced motion preference. One gotcha for anyone copying this: scroll-driven animations have to be written as longhands, or a minifier folds them into a shorthand that stable browsers reject.

sections.heading: Offline
sections.body: A service worker caches the core pages at install, fetches navigations network first so a new deploy is never served stale, and serves hashed assets cache first. The site installs, and there is a page for when the signal goes. The film frames stay online only.

sections.heading: The store
sections.body: The shelf is a static page with Stripe Elements in the browser. A Cloudflare Worker holds the catalogue, keeps the pictures in KV, and prices every order again from its own list, because nothing the page believes about money is trusted. It runs in test mode until it does not.

sections.heading: Machine readers
sections.body: There is an [llms.txt](/llms.txt), a [JSON Resume](/resume.json) that also renders the [resume page](/resume/), and schema.org data on the front page. Each page gets its own social card at build time, drawn on the drawing grid in the site's type by satori and rasterised by sharp, from the same list the site uses for titles. The [log](/log/) reads git during the build.

weightBody: Measured after every build: the HTML, the CSS and the script each page loads, gzipped as a browser would fetch them. Pictures, film frames and models are not counted. They are most of what you see and none of what this table is about.
